claim:
Text: "UNESCO declared Nadar community as the most ancient race in the world."
Claim author: Kumar Shankar
Claim date: October 31, 2020
before_justification: An exhaustive search of official UNESCO records, affiliated bodies, and related academic sources found no evidence of any declaration by UNESCO designating the Nadar community as the world's most ancient race. More significantly, UNESCO's own authoritative historical position, formalized in its [1950 Statement on Race](http://www.honestthinking.org/en/unesco/UNESCO.1950.Statement_on_Race.htm), explicitly refutes the scientific basis for ranking human groups by antiquity, stating that racial classifications are not static or hierarchical and that all humans belong to the same species.
after_justification: The claim that UNESCO declared the Nadar community as the most ancient race is refuted by the evidence. There is no official UNESCO statement, report, or declaration supporting this assertion, and the concept of designating a "most ancient race" is scientifically invalid and outside UNESCO's mandate. Fact-checking sources directly label the claim as false, and historical and anthropological evidence regarding the Nadar community's origins is uncertain and does not support the specific claim.

Nadar (also referred as Nadan, Shanar) is a caste of Tamil Nadu and Kerala in South India, and also of Sri Lanka.
Nadars are predominant in the southern districts of Tuticorin, Kaniyakumari, Tirunelveli and Virudhunagar.
The Nadar community was not a single caste, but developed from an assortment of related subcastes and classes of different origins, which in course of time, came under the single banner Nadar.
Nadar climbers are the largest subset of today’s Nadar community. A few subsects of the Nadar community, such as the Nelamaikkarars, were traditionally wealthy landlords and money lenders.
Historically, most Nadars were humble cultivators of palmyra trees and jaggery and a few were also involved in the toddy trade.
Nadar climbers had historically faced discrimination from major upper castes in some regions. The martial art of Southern Kalaripayattu was historically practiced by the Nadars.
In post-independence India, the Nadars have made significant strides through their emphasis on education and entrepreneurship.
The socio-economic development achieved by the Nadars in southern India has elicited academic interest.

Speaking at a conference organised by a caste group, Mr.Pandiarajan said the Nadar community has gained its uniqueness by its spirituality and its “sense of of business.”
“Every man has a DNA. Similarly, each community has its unique DNA, bequeathed over generations,” he said.
Pointing to the trade of jaggery 200 years ago, transporting the produce on donkeys to other settlements, Mr. Pandiarajan said the Nadar community had several symbols of unity.
“The community has built Badhrakali temples wherever they go. This has been a symbol of unity. The sense of spirituality is strong,” he said.
He cited examples of members of the community, such as Shiv Nadar, who developed one of the biggest IT companies in India with their “sense of business.”
